payload.acceptance_criteria:
A requirements v5 comment on basicly-qpr2xmr states that each adapter reports capability flags, that the orchestration code reads only those flags, and that a missing operation is refused by name.
The same comment states that each adapter has replay fixtures recorded from the real vendor client, and that they supplement the nightly live contract test.
The same comment states, under R2 or R7, that a session above the permission ceiling is refused by name before its first turn.
The comment cites docs/research/t3-code.md.
payload.description:
## Context
The T3 Code review (docs/research/t3-code.md, record basicly-upnhikm, checked 2026-11-19 at pingdotgg/t3code c5badf4e) found three patterns that requirements v4 lacks: adapters report capability flags that the code reads (Y1), adapter tests replay fixtures recorded from the real vendor client and supplement the nightly live test (Y2), and a permission ceiling refuses a turn above it by name (Y3). Decision D2 stays: T3 Code is a reference, not a dependency.
payload.title: Add capability flags, replay fixtures and a permission ceiling to meta harness requirements

When .basicly/ledger is the frozen marker, marker-families reads .basicly/ledger-archive and the local vault clone of the project's prefix, and names each store it read.
When .basicly/ledger is the frozen marker, ledger-bodies checks the archive and vault records of the project's prefix.
Both checks refuse a run that read zero records.
migrate --freeze removes snapshot.jsonl, checkpoint-*.jsonl and .events.lock before it archives the ledger, so ledger-archive holds only the fingerprinted source files
